filament.name: Amolen Glow in the Dark PLA

heroSummary: The Bambu Lab A1 prints Amolen Glow in the Dark PLA reliably at up to 167 mm/s based on a 14 mm³/s volumetric limit, but requires swapping the stock stainless steel nozzle for a hardened steel hotend to prevent rapid abrasive wear. The open-frame design is fully compatible with standard PLA bed temperatures (60°C) without needing an enclosure.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate cleaned with dish soap and warm water (no adhesive required)
slicerTweaks: Cap Maximum Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at speeds above 167 mm/s.
Increase wall line count to 3 or 4 to enhance phosphorescent glow brightness and intensity without compromising structural density.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' (Max detour length: 0) to minimize surface travel marks caused by abrasive particles trailing across outer perimeters.
Set Hotend Temperature to 215°C for all layers and Initial Layer Bed Temperature to 60°C to guarantee smooth flow and strong first-layer bonding.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Premature nozzle wear and uneven extrusion diameter
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Strontium aluminate phosphorescent particles in the filament severely abrade the stock Bambu Lab stainless steel nozzle orifice.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install the official Bambu Lab 0.4mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly and select the hardened nozzle option in the printer settings.

troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Amolen Glow PLA is hygroscopic and absorbs ambient humidity, resulting in moisture boil and oozing at the hotend.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the spool in a filament dryer at 50°C for 6 to 8 hours before printing, and verify retraction distance is tuned to 0.8 mm.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: First layer peeling or corner warping
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Contaminants such as finger oils on the Textured PEI Plate reduce adhesion for modified PLA formulations.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Scrub the textured PEI sheet thoroughly with warm water and degreasing dish soap, dry with an unwashed microfiber cloth, and increase bed temperature to 62°C.

faq.question: Can I print Amolen Glow in the Dark PLA with the stock Bambu A1 stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: No, printing glow-in-the-dark filament with stainless steel will enlarge the nozzle orifice within a few hundred grams of printing, degrading print quality and layer consistency; a hardened steel nozzle upgrade is required.

faq.question: Can I feed Amolen Glow PLA through the Bambu Lab AMS Lite?
faq.answer: Yes, but prolonged use will cause gradual wear on the AMS Lite feeder funnels and PTFE tubes due to abrasive particles; inspect feeding components periodically for grooving.

faq.question: Why does my print glow faintly compared to the product photos?
faq.answer: Phosphorescent glow relies on volume and wall thickness; increasing outer walls to 3 or 4 and utilizing 20%+ gyroid infill dramatically amplifies light storage compared to thin single-wall prints.

faq.question: Does printing Amolen Glow PLA on the Bambu A1 require an enclosure?
faq.answer: No, Glow PLA prints best in an open-air environment with standard cooling (80-100%); an enclosure can cause heat creep and clogging in the direct drive toolhead.
